title: Korean Tteok & Spicy Pork "Ragù"
imagePrompt: Ivory-white rice cakes glisten with a deep rust-red and brown sauce, each piece coated in the thick, glossy ragù so that the color clings in lacquered folds. Crumbles of cooked ground pork are visible throughout, intermingled with wilted bok choy whose dark-green leaves contrast against the sauce. A scattering of bright-green garlic chives tops the dish, and the overall surface looks richly sauced, slightly shiny, and deeply colored from the gochujang and black bean sauce.
subtitle: with Baby Bok Choy

ingredients.heading: Ingredients
ingredients.note: A Korean-style ragù—2 lb ground pork simmered in an aromatic, spiced sauce tossed with soft rice cakes and tender baby bok choy. Scaled for 6.
items: 2 lb ground pork
1 lb 10 oz Korean rice cakes (tteok)
13 oz baby bok choy
3 bunches garlic chives
3 medium yellow onions
3-inch piece fresh ginger
6½ tbsp black bean sauce
6½ tbsp crème fraîche
3 tbsp gochujang
3 tbsp soy glaze
2 tbsp oil
1⅔ cups water (for the sauce)
Salt and pepper to taste
ingredients.callout: Gochujang note: Start with 1½ tbsp and add more to taste—this Korean red chili paste brings the heat. You’ll have 3 tbsp total if you want it spicy.

body.html: A Korean-style ragù—2 lb ground pork cooked down in an aromatic, spiced sauce with ginger, onion, and garlic chives, then tossed with soft rice cakes (tteok) and tender baby bok choy. Finished with crème fraîche and soy glaze. This batch serves 6.

items: Mise en place — wash, chop, and measure everything (15 min)
Cook the pork — brown 2 lb ground pork in a wide pot
Build flavor — add ginger, onion, garlic chives, bok choy
Finish — simmer rice cakes in the sauce until coated (35–45 min cook)

body.html: Pro tip: Use a Dutch oven or 12-inch skillet. Two pounds of pork will steam in a small pan—you want room to brown, not stew.

items: Set a large pot of salted water on to boil (you’ll need room for 1 lb 10 oz rice cakes later).
Wash and dry all fresh produce.
Peel and mince the 3-inch piece of ginger.
Thinly slice all 3 bunches of garlic chives. Set 1½ bunches aside for garnish.
Peel and small-dice the 3 onions.
Roughly chop the bok choy, keeping stems and leaves separate.
Measure the sauces into small bowls: 6½ tbsp black bean sauce, 6½ tbsp crème fraîche, 3 tbsp soy glaze, and 3 tbsp gochujang.
Have the 2 lb pork and rice cakes at the station. Measure 1⅔ cups water for the sauce.

body.html: Mise en place: Don’t turn on the pork pan until every bowl is filled. This batch moves fast once the meat is in.

items: Heat a Dutch oven or 12-inch skillet (nonstick is fine) over medium heat.
Add 2 tbsp oil. Once hot, add the 2 lb ground pork.
Season with salt and pepper. Cook for 8–12 minutes, frequently breaking the meat apart with a spoon.
Cook until browned and cooked through. If the pan is crowded and the pork is steaming, work in two batches and return it all to the pot.

body.html: Browning, not steaming: Leave the pork alone for a minute at a time so it can color. Two pounds needs space and a little patience.

items: To the pot of cooked pork, add the minced ginger, diced onion, and 1½ bunches of garlic chives (the other half is for garnish).
Cook, stirring occasionally, for 4–5 minutes until the onion is softened and fragrant.

slides.title: Finish the Ragù
slides.checkboxLabel: Sauce thickened and coating the pork

items: To the pot, add the bok choy, black bean sauce, crème fraîche, soy glaze, and 1⅔ cups water.
Add 1½ tbsp gochujang to start (you can add the remaining 1½ tbsp for extra spice).
Stir to combine. Simmer, stirring occasionally, for 6–8 minutes until the sauce has thickened and coats the pork.

body.html: Spice control: Taste as you go. Add more gochujang ½ tbsp at a time if you like more heat. You have 3 tbsp total.

items: While the ragù simmers, add the rice cakes to the pot of boiling water. Stir so they don’t stick.
Cook for 2–3 minutes, or until tender. Drain thoroughly.
Transfer the cooked rice cakes to the pot of ragù.
Season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 3–4 minutes until the rice cakes are thoroughly coated.
Remove from heat and season again to taste.
Divide the finished ragù and rice cakes between 6 bowls.
Garnish with the remaining 1½ bunches of garlic chives.
Enjoy!
Optional toppings: sesame seeds, a fried egg, extra gochujang, kimchi, or toasted nori
